title: POC Weekly Sync - Rollout & Go-Live Planning
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on rollout and go-live plan. Agreed on a staged canary (5% -> 20% -> 100%) with A/B for two gating KPIs (p95 latency and QA score). Action items: Redwood to share canary script and monitoring runbook; Acme to schedule dry-run and allocate SRE for cutover window. Security team requested KMS and audit-log examples; Redwood to provide docs.
next_steps: Alex to send canary rollout script + example runbook by 2026-06-05
Acme to schedule a dry-run with SRE for 2026-06-10 window
Priya to run internal benchmark with 95th-percentile traffic profile and share results by 2026-06-08
Rosa to confirm KMS provider details and required docs by 2026-06-07
action_items: Alex Martinez - Share canary rollout script and monitoring runbook - 2026-06-05
Priya Desai - Export load test logs and p95 latency snapshots for current pilot - 2026-06-08
Jared Liu - Allocate SRE for dry-run and provide cutover window - 2026-06-04
Rosa Gomez - List compliance checklist items required for Private deployment (KMS, audit log retention) - 2026-06-07
Maya Patel - Validate network egress rules and VPC peering steps for cutover - 2026-06-08
transcript:
00:00 - Alex Martinez: okay hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is our weekly poc check-in focused on the rollout and go-live plan. i think we have the same agenda — quick status, canary strategy, monitoring, runbooks, and security before we wrap with next steps.
00:45 - Jared Liu: yea thanks alex. quick update from our side — pilot has been running for two weeks, we've ramped to about 10k requests/day, latency looks ok on average but p95 spikes during peak auth-batch.
03:12 - Priya Desai: when you say p95 spikes, are those at higher sequence lengths or are they KV cache misses? sometimes the kayvee cache warm-up causes a bunch of cold-start latency.
05:10 - Maya Patel: it's mostly during end-of-day settlement jobs, sequences are longer and we see higher memory pressure on the dedicated pool. we did a quick trace and there are a few cases where the model falls back to a smaller variant which increased tokenization overhead.
10:22 - Alex Martinez: ok that's good to know. for the rollout plan i was thinking a staged canary: start at 5% traffic for 2 hours, check p95 and error rate, then 20% for a day, then 100% if no regressions. we should also run an A/B where 50/50 traffic for a subset of routes to compare quality metrics — especially the QA score you mentioned in week 1.
18:05 - Jared Liu: 5% for 2 hours seems low — our traffic is pretty spiky, does that give us enough signal? maybe do synthetic traffic during the 2 hours to accelerate signal?
18:35 - Priya Desai: yes synthetic load is fine; we'll provide a load script. also recommend running canary during low business impact window plus run synthetic bursts to hit p95.
20:40 - Rosa Gomez: security question — during canary and cutover, what stays in our VPC? we need to ensure no model artifacts leave the private subnets; also KMS integration for key rotation and audit logging, SOC2 mentions, etc.
22:00 - Alex Martinez: good call. Redwood Private preserves data in your VPC and supports customer-managed KMS. we'll send the KMS integration guide and sample audit logs. note: transcriber sometimes says "Redwood Dedicate" instead of Dedicated, sorry for that.
25:00 - Maya Patel: A/B tests — how do we measure quality? we run labeled evaluation set but in production we need user-facing signals. Jared — can you provide acceptance thresholds?
26:10 - Jared Liu: acceptance thresholds: p95 latency under 450ms on average across canary traffic, error rate <0.5%, and quality score no worse than -1 point relative to baseline on our internal QA set. also no spike in user-facing failure rate.
30:15 - Priya Desai: we can gate on those. technical detail: for canary routing we'll use smart routing to pin traffic by route and use automatic fallback to a smaller model variant in the event of capacity issues. we will instrument both model-level metrics and application-level metrics.
32:15 - Maya Patel: monitoring — what dashboards do we need? need per-route p95, median, token throughput, error rate, and also a quality delta comparison for A/B. alerting thresholds: p95 > 450ms for 10 minutes, error-rate > 0.5% for 5 minutes, quality delta worse by >1.5 points.
35:00 - Priya Desai: i'll assemble an example dashboard and alert policy. we'll include synthetic canary checks that simulate user flows and validate completeness.
36:30 - Rosa Gomez: one more security point — we need to capture audit logs in a format our SIEM ingests, retention at least 13 months, and show proof of key rotation.
38:30 - Alex Martinez: noted, we'll attach sample audit log dumps and KMS rotation docs in the follow-up.
40:05 - Jared Liu: rollback plan? what's the fastest way to cut traffic back to the previous model and ensure state (tokens/KV cache) doesn't cause inconsistencies?
41:20 - Priya Desai: rollback is basically a routing flip with immediate fallback; we keep the previous model in the pool for 30 minutes post-cutover. KV cache inconsistency is rare if we do route-level pinning — but we'll clear prefix caches as part of rollback steps in the runbook.
43:00 - Alex Martinez: Decision: go with staged canary 5% (2 hours + synthetic), 20% (24 hours), then 100% with the A/B running in parallel for two days on critical routes. Gate: p95 <450ms, error-rate <0.5%, quality delta <= -1 point.
44:10 - Maya Patel: agree. i'll schedule dry-run with SRE for 2026-06-10 and allocate ops for the cutover window.
44:50 - Alex Martinez: Great — recap: Alex to send canary script and runbook, Priya to share dashboard and benchmarks, Acme to confirm SRE window and KMS info. thanks everyone, we'll sync next week same time.
notes: Decision: staged canary and A/B gating described above
Redwood to provide KMS integration guide and audit log examples
Dry-run scheduled (proposed) for 2026-06-10 — Acme to confirm
